The worst of the Dark Souls series and one of the worst action RPG experiences I've ever had. Being a big fan of action RPGs and having played a ridiculous amount of games in my life, I can confidently say this is without a doubt the most frustrating, poorly designed mess of a game I ever had the misfortunate of playing. The balance of the game is completely broken, mechanically the game takes a step back from it's predecessor, enemies have infinite stamina and swing around like crazy with 8 hit combos and massive reach, crowds of smaller enemies will easily corner you and deal massive damage compared to their little size, gank boss fights far too many times, weapons and armor that the design discourages the player from using or is completely useless. Seriously, the list of flaws go on forever.
Don't take this review as a "this is too hard for me" complaint, i'm trying to be as objective as possible here. I played and beat Demons Souls back when that first came out and i enjoyed the challenge of that game. Beat it several times with different builds each time. Than i completed Dark Souls 1 and thought it was one of the best Action RPGs of all time, despite it's many problems (mostly performance releated). I even put up with the lack luster world and design of Dark Souls 2 and completed that game enough times to the point where i can run through the game SL1 within a few hours.
But than we get to Dark Souls 3 and it just seems like a huge middle finger to me. I am shocked that this game comes from the same developers as the first game. I cannot see a single similarity design-wise. Sure, they throw in tons of "references" and by that I mean copy characters and enemies from the previous games and paste them in their for no reason. The first game had purpose and intent to it's design, mechanics and levels that were built to support that vision. Dark Souls 3 has no idea what it's doing. It feels extremely rushed and was likely designed in chunks, where different members of the team worked separately on different chunks and in the end they just mashed it together without giving a f***.
I could sit here all day and pick apart the details but others have already done that before me and it wouldn't really change anyone opinion. If you enjoyed this game, im surprised but also very curious as to how anybody could find any entertainment in this experience. Even after completeing the entire game, every boss, and the 1st dlc, I really had to force myself through it and i felt no sense of reward for the accomplishment. The game is cheap, hard for the sake of hard, and not in a clever way but in a brutally unfair way. When you win, you don't feel like you outsmarted or outskilled your opponents, you feel like you got lucky or exploited the games bad design to get through areas in a way that must not have been intended.
The base game is bad but it's playable. The game really drops it's last turd with the pair of DLC areas. The 1st one is just tedious and boring. The 2nd one is so bad that it definitely gets a number on my Top 10 Worst Levels of All Time list. I'm glad this series is finally over. From Software has learned nothing over the years, either that or they just don't care to put in the time and effort to make a quality gaming experience. Bugs that have been around for years haven't been fixed, butchered mechanics and progressively worse design make From Software a really confusing developer to follow.
Anyway that's about all I need to say. This isn't much of a review, it's ranty and unorganized but I think that fits this game perfectly. 4/10 ~ only play if you are into punishing yourself.

I got around to trying Fallout 4 with the recent free weekend and was pleasantly surprised. I am enjoying it much more then either Fallout 3 or Skyrim, for different sets of reasons. Is it "Skyrim with guns"? Yes, very much so. However, the general feel of the game is much better for me. It suffers from a similar but lesser degree of bloat and mid-game drag, being entirely too long and inconsistently paced for much of my 80+ hours. The load times factored into this considerably, but it runs more smoothly then any Bethesda game I've played before, and it's nice to hear my character talk. I got lucky in most cases as regards to bugs, though an issue loading saves near the very end of the game caused me a bit of a scare.
You are the "Sole Survivor," an inhabitant of the Vault 111 fallout shelter who flees the onset of nuclear armageddon in 2077, only to awaken 200 years later, with their spouse murdered and infant son missing. So begins a desperate search through the wasteland known as the Commonwealth, consisting of the ruins of Boston and its environs. In your search you inevitably become a central figure in the lives of many of this region's citizens, and ulitmately a war for its control and answers to world-shaking questions: What measure is a non-human? Where do you stand on the scale between freedom and security? What are you willing to do not only to survive, but to thrive, to win? The game is not only open-ended but very morally gray, and wether your choices were right or not is left up to your own interpretation. This is a stark contrast to Fallout 3, which at least from where I was standing concerned a benevolent chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel waging a war for freedom against the totalitarian Enclave.
People say the conversations in this game are a little too Mass Effect, but I think it works just fine. It's also sometimes a lot easier to tell at a glance what your character is actually going to say, barring the wildcard "Sarcastic" responses. The companion system is entertaining but far less sophsiticated then most other RPGs, with limited dialogue opporutnities and wildy varying combat effectiveness for each character. I found myself quite partial to Curie, whose excessive adorability, gifts of Stimpaks, devotion to scientific progress and surprising fighting ability endeared her to me quickly.
The shooting, particularly when using VATS, is enjoyable, especially when your Luck perks sucessfully proc, and there is a satisfying array of guns of all types and calibers, which can be customized to your liking. However, coming from something like Borderlands, Battleborn or Killing Floor 2, the combat overall feels a bit stiff and clunky, and it still seems like you are required to use VATS to succeed in at least some fights, as in Fallout 3. The game's difficulty can also feel a tad erratic- you can tear through a number of engagements before unceremoniously being disintegrated by a nuclear Fat Man shell, which apparently warrented its own achievement.
I can't help but love that there is actually a use for all the junk you find lying around in these sorts of games. I find it amusing you're given Power Armor virtually from the get go, though maintaining it seems to be a much more involved process. You're not only encouraged to grab everything you can find, but rewarded with experience points for using it to craft modifcations for your gear and upgrade friendly towns with new stuff- at last, the packrat in me finds vindication. The series seems to be gradually approaching the status of a functional FPS, though that is a far cry from its original form and I am left to wonder. It's a competently executed FPS/RPG, especially compared to its immediate predecessor, but is it really Fallout? That, I regret to say, is not my place to judge.

Still in beta but is already amazing. It's quite like Terraria, but with more NPC's, a lot more area to explore, more complex character creation and SPACE! I really recommend buying this if you enjoy/enjoyed Terraria.

Even though the game now guides you almost completely through, it still has a lot of freedom because of the massive amount of randomly generated planets that you can explore. Great game, till they decided we had too much fun. Now u can almost only get negative stats on your heroes. Was fun before, cant recommend it any longer, havent played it after the Devs ruined the game.
Details:
First it was a real fun game, where you had to grind your way through with stressed out, ill and kleptomanic heroes. Even the the items you got always had a negative impact as well. So it really took time to somehow protect your most beloved hereos through the dungeons and get family heirlooms now and then to finally upgrade your buildings.
Slowly but steadily you would get one or two heroes to the next level without them having 10 different negative effects at once, making them unplayable. Then you finally upgraded the armory and you would spend hours to get enough money to get your top group of heroes new weapons.
Combine this with completely different hero classes that all have their unique purposes and u had a hell of a fun game. At least for me as a RPG fan by heart.
Now, what changed: First, they limited the positive quirks each and every hero can have to 5, which means, that from my best heroes 70% of their positive stats just vanished. It really takes time to build a strong hero in the game and the quirks are the only way to improve them once they got a top weapon and armor. So now it just doesn't make fun anymore playing your best heroes, because you will hit the top ceiling and that's it.
Moreover they didn't limit the negative quirks. While u can't make your heroes better, they will become worse and worse if you don't pay hefty gold for it.
And finally they installed a corpse system which makes absolutely zero sense at all. A 8 HP monster  leaves a 15hp corpse behind (WTF?!) which just blocks your way from attacking the other monsters (which still can attack you) and just prolongs fights for no reason.
Given the fact that you can't boost your hereos anymore and regarding the dragging fights with the corpses I can't recommend the game anymore.
Edit: The negative quirks are limited to 5 now. Still, no more fun till the remove the limit of the positive ones again.

After playing the game when it came out on my friend's computer, I quickly sunk several hours into the game. Eventually, I stopped because I was bored of the game. When the game was available free over a weekend, I decided to jump in and see if the game could pull me back in and I would finally sink money into the purchase of Fallout 4. However, I will not be buying Fallout 4. Upon playing again and from my past experience, several issues stick out:
1. I didn't care about a single character in this game. This still holds true. When your spouse is killed across from you in the cryochamber, I didn't even bat an eye. The reality is: people in Fallout games facing struggle and death have no impact on me because it is common for them. That is one of the points of Fallout. People in that world face struggles and death daily. I need more than some city slick ghoul killing someone in front of me for me to have any attachment to them, even if that is suppose to be some sense of fear. I mean, you can blow up Megaton, a large settlement in Fallout 3, killing a multitude of citizens within the first couple hours. I'm not asking for the ability to play God with people in Fallout 4, but I just need more character depth than what we are provided.
2. The settlement builder lacks any satisfaction. This is worse since I didn't care about any of the settlers thanks to that glorious onslaught of quests asking me to save some settlement.
3. Lack of impactful morality system. You will usually get what you want among the empathetic, apathetic, good or evil routes. However, this system has taken more than enough beatings from other reviewers.
4. Everything is just...bland. The only thing drawing me to the bland buildings, cities and other landmarks is simply because I was to escape the bland, barren wastelands. I have no fear for large raider camps simply because I want to be involved in something other than sprinting across the wastes. I replace one bland thing for a slightly more interesting bland thing, but the only time I ever stop and say "wow, this is cool" was when I visited the synth homebase. That's it.
5. Nothing feels more like a kick in the groin than when they release you from the awful vault tutorial to a world that feels open and a place you can explore just about most things - and then you get to your second town, Concord, a place where mostly everything is boarded up.
One positive thing: they nail the gunplay compared to Fallout 3 and NV imo. Everything kicks and feels good to use.
-------
TL;DR
Played it once then again recently. Failed to be drawn back in due to a bland world, lacking morality alignments and decision making and inabiltiy to care for any characters in that world. Gunplay is better than previous Fallout games.

In a world where "story on rails," handholding, and "easy mode" difficulties have become the norm, it is refreshing to discover a game that will kick your♥♥♥♥♥and not apologize for it.
On its surface, Darkest Dungeon appears to be a simple turn based RPG dungeon crawler.  The notion of "simple" is quickly discarded as you will be quickly bombarded with the possibility of very deep strategy as well as events taht will force you to think on the move.
The game greatly appeals to the senses.  From its unique dark fantasy art to its dynamically changing music and sound fx that will have you wondering if you are going as insane as your party of adventures, the atmosphere of game delivers big time.  The mechanics of combat combined with the visuals and audio deliver some of the most satisfying as well as most heartbreaking moments of any combat based game.
This game is not for those who need to have their hands held through an adventure.  You will fail.  You may very well likely fail in a way that the best option is to restart from the beginning.  However, if you are able to keep your ego and confidence in check, you will find a truly entertaining game wrapped up in a simple yet compelling story that will have you begging for more abuse.

Fallout 4 is…
Damn. What is Fallout 4? Has an obsession with ‘features’ undermined the series?
Todd Howard is a forward thinker, there’s no doubt about that; always looking to drive the games he helms to be ‘bigger and better’ than the last. Unfortunately, like all good things taken too far in the one direction, this urge to be ‘better’ can yield some unpleasant results. Howard’s eye for innovation has led to a number of improvements over F4’s predecessor – namely in the smoother controls and gunplay, and streamlined inventory management. In its favour, Fallout 4 is far more user-friendly than its predecessors, and this is a great thing if you can travel back in your mind and remember how clunky each previous Bethesda game is. Fallout 4 also boasts an overarching narrative that is one of the most resonant of any game in the series so far, balancing existential themes with a deeply personal story that holds some truly powerful emotional moments.
And yet somehow, in saying that, Fallout 4 feels like the most soulless Fallout game so far. How did this happen?
I for one believe that in the pursuit of topping the aesthetic and superficial achievements of previous Bethesda games like Skyrim and Fallout 3, Bethesda have unfortunately focused on the wrong elements to innovate, and have left the things that make Fallout ‘Fallout’ by the wayside.
Whilst F4 is indeed eminently more playable than F3, New Vegas, or even Skyrim, the streamlining of the combat mechanics and subsequently overwhelming focus on gunplay has robbed the game of its flexibility. Nine times out of ten, the solution to any problem will be ‘shoot a thing’, and while the option is still available to talk your way out of some situations, there’s a distinct lack of nuance that only became glaring to me in retrospect; sure, you can tread through the game easily enough, and maybe you’ll have fun, you might even be impressed at times, but you might also, like me, find yourself at a point feeling a little bored. You might not know why, you might not even explicitly know that you’re bored, but for some reason you don’t feel the compulsion to play that you used to - the excitement – and I believe that this is down to the fact that F4 is far less an RPG than any of the other Fallout game, rather it is, more than anything else, a base-building FPS in an open world.
And you can get a base-building open world FPS game elsewhere. The uniqueness of Fallout is in its one-of-a-kind atmosphere, the tongue-in-cheek humour, the secrets and surprises that lay hiding around the world, waiting to be stumbled upon, and the feeling that in making choices, you’re never making things perfect; you’re making friends and enemies, and changing the world before you. I don’t play Fallout in order to check off all the settlements I’ve liberated, or the areas I’ve wiped clean of enemies. I play it for the things I miss the first time and discover on a later play-through. In my second play-through of F4, I realised that I’d found almost everything there was to see; I’d been to almost all of the locations, killed the inhabitants, looted the chests and left, and in the places I hadn’t found, killing something and looting a chest was about all there was to do. I knew what the alternate endings to the path I trod before were because the two options had been lain out before me the last time I went through. And in finishing the story, there were no unexpected surprises – things didn’t change much following my choice, and certainly not in an unpredictable way. So gone are the days of a unique and interesting ethical greyness of the post-apocalypse. Gone are ambiguous moral choices, in which you have to make a personal judgement without knowing what the explicit outcome of your actions will be.
Fallout 4 is a shoot-em-up. You simply can’t finish the game without killing, and even when attempting a positive moral play-through in which you treat the characters benevolently and help out as many people as you can, you will leave a swath of hundreds, if not thousands of humans, mutants, and animals dead in your wake. Most of the beings you stumble upon will be hostile, and regardless of which pathway you choose in the end, you’re a destroyer first and foremost.
And thus F4 betrays the ethos of the Fallout series. It’s a long way from the living, breathing wastelands of F1, 2, and NV - from a world that is bigger than you. Yes, you can build a base, and outfit it with a bunch of sweet attractions and weapons. Yes, the movement and shooting is more fun. Yes, it looks better than the last gen games. But where’s the heart? Where’s the sense of immersion? Between all the systems and gimmicks and repeating quests that pop up again and again into infinity, where’s the feeling that you’re in a world in which the people have complex problems? Where’s the compromise? Where are the solutions that in and of themselves can cause unseen problems of their own? There’s a side mission that involves a cowardly shrinking violet who needs some confidence, and I kid you not, this scenario is resolved by dragging him along to a shootout, after which he finds the strength within himself to live life to the fullest. Legitimately. You give a sad loner confidence by taking the guy to kill some people. This is perfectly indicative of the perspective the game takes – all your problems are solved by bloodshed. That’s not the way a believable world works. That’s not what makes a Fallout game interesting.
Perhaps this seems unfair, because I’ve given worse games a better rating, but I can’t really be okay with giving my recommendation to a game that loses sight of the things so core to the unique successes of the franchise. Fallout 4 isn’t a bad game, but it fails at being a good Fallout game.

The worst of the Dark Souls series and one of the worst action RPG experiences I've ever had. Being a big fan of action RPGs and having played a ridiculous amount of games in my life, I can confidently say this is without a doubt the most frustrating, poorly designed mess of a game I ever had the misfortunate of playing. The balance of the game is completely broken, mechanically the game takes a step back from it's predecessor, enemies have infinite stamina and swing around like crazy with 8 hit combos and massive reach, crowds of smaller enemies will easily corner you and deal massive damage compared to their little size, gank boss fights far too many times, weapons and armor that the design discourages the player from using or is completely useless. Seriously, the list of flaws go on forever.
Don't take this review as a "this is too hard for me" complaint, i'm trying to be as objective as possible here. I played and beat Demons Souls back when that first came out and i enjoyed the challenge of that game. Beat it several times with different builds each time. Than i completed Dark Souls 1 and thought it was one of the best Action RPGs of all time, despite it's many problems (mostly performance releated). I even put up with the lack luster world and design of Dark Souls 2 and completed that game enough times to the point where i can run through the game SL1 within a few hours.
But than we get to Dark Souls 3 and it just seems like a huge middle finger to me. I am shocked that this game comes from the same developers as the first game. I cannot see a single similarity design-wise. Sure, they throw in tons of "references" and by that I mean copy characters and enemies from the previous games and paste them in their for no reason. The first game had purpose and intent to it's design, mechanics and levels that were built to support that vision. Dark Souls 3 has no idea what it's doing. It feels extremely rushed and was likely designed in chunks, where different members of the team worked separately on different chunks and in the end they just mashed it together without giving a f***.
I could sit here all day and pick apart the details but others have already done that before me and it wouldn't really change anyone opinion. If you enjoyed this game, im surprised but also very curious as to how anybody could find any entertainment in this experience. Even after completeing the entire game, every boss, and the 1st dlc, I really had to force myself through it and i felt no sense of reward for the accomplishment. The game is cheap, hard for the sake of hard, and not in a clever way but in a brutally unfair way. When you win, you don't feel like you outsmarted or outskilled your opponents, you feel like you got lucky or exploited the games bad design to get through areas in a way that must not have been intended.
The base game is bad but it's playable. The game really drops it's last turd with the pair of DLC areas. The 1st one is just tedious and boring. The 2nd one is so bad that it definitely gets a number on my Top 10 Worst Levels of All Time list. I'm glad this series is finally over. From Software has learned nothing over the years, either that or they just don't care to put in the time and effort to make a quality gaming experience. Bugs that have been around for years haven't been fixed, butchered mechanics and progressively worse design make From Software a really confusing developer to follow.
Anyway that's about all I need to say. This isn't much of a review, it's ranty and unorganized but I think that fits this game perfectly. 4/10 ~ only play if you are into punishing yourself.

Game mechanics are still unbalanced in my opinion.
Stress builds up way too fast without a reliable healing method - one stressed character often causes a chain reaction to ramp the stress for the party up to +30 a turn.
HP heal is also poorly designed. The only way to heal is in-combat as each food heals only one HP. Having to grind 5 mins in a combat by chain-stunning an enemy is not the way to go. Also, there are not enough stun and heal skills to reliably pull this off early-game.
Items are way too expensive. The item pouch is too small, given the plethora of mechanics in this game (torch level, stress, bleed, blight, HP, artifact cleansing, path clearing, etc). Even after ending a dungeon, players should be able to keep the items for the next quest.
The combat mechanics are too RNG-based, rather than skill-based. Opponents seem to dodge a significantly larger amount than the player.
Keep in mind that the villains' attacks also out-hit the players in HP and stress, which makes it tough as you will need to heal for two categories at a large cost.

Darkest Dungeon is a side-scrolling (that is, you scroll from side to side in one dimention) role playing game set in a world of dread. Taking nods from Poe and Lovecraft, Darkest Dungeon does an amazing job at setting up an atmosphere that feels positively DARK. Everything in the game is designed around this focal point; that the game should cause dread in the hearts of its players, from the art style, to the sound design, to the dialogue, all the way down to the classes in the game. You as the player are on a quest to reclaim your family mansion after a dark and nameless evil put it to ruin. You have a town at the bottom of a hill looking up towards your mansion where you can upgrade certain buildings that provide relief or upgrades to your party. Your party consists of brave adventurers you recruit (for free), from palidans to witch doctors to bounty hunters. Each member has qwuirks, good and bad, that stay with them and affect their stats or behavior. A god-fearing man will only relieve stress at the church (as opposed to the tavern), a known-cheat cannot gamble to releive stress, and a kleptomaniac is liken to steal loot from you. Stress is a 0 to 200 variable along side a character's health. When their health reaches zero, they arrive at "Death's Door", suffer huge stat penalties, and have a chance of being killed off if they take damage. Stress, on the other hand, is an instant fatality if it reaches 200. Many events in the game can cause stress, from a sprung trap to an attack from enemies that does low damage, but high stress. When your characters reach 100 stress, their will is tested. There is a chance they will gain a buff and reduce their stress (this can be very powerful), but MOST OFTEN, they become paranoid, or fearful, or one of a multitude of negative effects that can cause extra stress on the party or flat out injure themselves. As your party adventures through dungeons, you will become VERY familiar with a "death spiral". Things will seem okay, except that one guy that has 90 stress. Then, he takes major stress damage from a nasty enemy critical strike, he becomes "abusive" and hurls insults at party members just about any time an action is taken. The stress accumulates across the board, soon your entire party is tested, bickering amongst themselves, refusing the fight, all the while monsters are STILL attacking them. Before you know it, they've all hit 200 stress and died, and your quest is at a loss. This you will become familiar with. Characters are free to recruit, but only a handful are available each week, and you MUST embark on an adventure for other characters to relieve stress, heal wounds, and cure diseases. Darkest Dungeon is very much like a rogue-like. The game encourages retreat, quest abandonment, and even starting over. It's brutal, and gamers who like to be punished will very much enjoy this game. Gamers who like brutality less, but love the eldritch, lovecraftian, madness-inducing atmosphere may also feel right at home. If you like both, WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR?
P.S. As far as "Early Access" goes, nothing feels particularly unfinished, save the "will be added later" dungeons. new classes are introduced every once in awhile, and I think playing it in early access WONT kill your fun before it's finished. You don't need to wait.

There are a LOT of "Most Helpful" reviews on this game right now that are in the red and that's not really fair, so I'd like to pitch in my two cents.  Time of writing is 8-11-2015, with the "Cove" area only just now being teased at an up-coming convention.
The two major things that people are harping on is the RNG and the newest "Corpse" mechanic.  I'll get into the corpse thing first, after a short bit of back-story.  If you can't be bothered to read through all of this, go ahead and skip to the bottom.  I won't hold it against you.
I got back into Darkest Dungeon quite a while ago.  I believe my heroes were all around the level 2-3 range when the corpse mechanic hit.  For those new to the game, that's about the area where larger / more dangerous enemies with new mechanics you haven't seen yet start popping up and where having your heroes skills and equipment being updated as best as you can starts to make a big difference.  You CAN get by without upgrading any of their stuff till about level two.  After that, if you still haven't upgraded any of their skills or armor or weapons, then you seriously should start doing that.
Anyways, I ended up having to re-adjust my parties whenever I wandered into dungeons now.  Damage Over time effects (DOT) where now much more important, as many larger and more heavily armored enemies (indicated by how much Protection or PROT they had) were much easier to kill with them.  The reason for that being DOT effects completely bypass PROT.  Also, corpses don't appear if a target dies to a Bleed or Blight effect.
And therein lies the start of the "problem" everyone has.  If you have bleeds or blights stacked on an enemy, but end up killing it with any other kind of attack, then a corpse happens.  Corpses do nothing except waste your time and take up the same amount of space as the enemy you just killed.  So if you kill something that takes up two spaces, the corpse will as well.
This is where people get angry, but I'm going to defend the company for this change.  Like others, I was actually breezing through this game.  It became hilariously easy, once you had some time invested, to just brute force your way through most fights, bosses not withstanding as they're more of a puzzle you need to figure out.
See, corpses are easier to clear than people give them crap for.  A few heroes (The Occultist, Leper, and Plague Doctor all spring to mind) have a move you can use (if you equipped them with it) that lets you clear all corpses on the field, regardless of where they are, in a single move.  Poof.  Gone.
Or you could just beat the corpses into nothingness (although you can still "miss" hitting them, somehow.)  Or you could just stack a couple bleeds / blights on them and take care of them that way.  Or, and this is the least efficient, wait them out, as they will eventually disappear on their own, but only after roughly four turns, which is not worth it if "Skeleton Mc. Shoots Your Face" is still in the back couple of spots and is hitting your heroes in the face with well placed crits and generally being kind of a jerk.
Finally, you COULD just MOVE the enemy from where they're standing to closer to the front, if you're having THAT much trouble.  Heroes that spring to mind are the Occultist, Bounty Hunter, Plague Doctor.  These three can be equipped with abilities that either pull enemies forward two spots (The Occultist and Bounty Hunter) or "shuffle" the enemy you hit into another spot (Bounty Hunter again and Plague Doctor).  While "shuffling" an enemy around isn't exactly an exact science (Except for the Plague Doctor, as her "shuffle enemy" button also clears all corpses on the field) it does still allow you to re-position any enemies that might be hanging out in the back rows.
And let me tell you, getting the drop on a group of skeletons and pulling that friggin "I throw wine at you which make your heroes freak out" to the front reduces him to trying to shank your heroes with a dinky knife and it is not NEARLY as effective.
Second, there's the RNG of this game and I promise to try and get through this part faster.  Without RNG, this game would fall apart.  With proper planning, hero skill management, and a few helpful trinkets, I've had little trouble clearing dungeons.
Most recently, one of my two Plague Doctors bit the dust and it hurt.  Completely my fault as I had no dedicated "healer" for that run.  It had hurt MORE because I thought I had lost the two valuable trinkets I had equipped her with, but after the fight was over, they dropped as loot.  That softened the blow considerably.  Sure losing the hero sucked too, but that's the thing.  They're SUPPOSED to be expendable.  Go to the caravan wagon.  Pick out another Plague Doctor with decent starter stuff.  Train them up.  Boom, replaced.  Losing the trinkets (one of which was VERY RARE and I only had one of) would have hurt more.
RNG made me lose a hero as I couldn't throw a heal at her in time and the hidden roll to decide if she stayed on death's door or bit the dust said "You lose".  But as painful as that was, I knew I could recover.  Heroes are free.  I've gotten most my hamlet up to max (minus the camping lady on the edge of town, but not from a lack of trying) and I STILL want to keep playing this game.
TL;DR:  You should get this game.  I've not had much experience with "Roguelike" types of games before and I love this thing.  The art style is amazing.  I never get tired of hearing the narrator.  The music is incredible (and even changes depending on how much light you have going).  Every hero has a spot in the team. (Arguable, but still.  People hate the Leper.  Gear and train him.  Then watch him DESTROY things on your behalf.)  Think things through.  You KNOW there's going to be corpses.  Bring people who can deal with it.  Mix ranged into your lineup.  Be prepared for everything to go pear shaped.
And ALWAYS BRING SHOVELS.
Now get out there.  Those dungeons aren't going to clear themselves.  There's loot to find.  Walking corpses to put down.  And an endless stream of eager heroes at your disposal.  Use them.  Good luck.

This game could well have been one of the best there is, but it's simply not.
Design, concept, and even the level of difficulty is just perfect and adds up to make for a really good game, if only...
If only there was some slightest resemblance of tactics to it that would actually matter to the game play whatsoever!
In the end of the day it all comes down to pure, basic luck whether you make it through even your very first dungeon at all.
Every single attempt of making up a strategy will simply result in nothing but frustration as your characters get pummelled by the lowliest of enemies avaible. And in the same way, your worst attempt ever at making a fully functional party may well come out on top and completely unharmed.
There is simply no consistency to this at all, and it seems like the very design - and not just the gloomy story - has been specifically created to bring you down.
It's one thing to make a game that's simply difficult to master, and something else entirely to make this difficulty simply based on whether your characters are lucky to survive a hit that can range from anywhere between 1 and 21 in damage, or simply happen to get "ambushed" by an enemy that you're already perfectly aware of...
On the other hand, if you actually enjoy being utterly frustrated, or simply want to test your luck at games, then this just might be able to pick your interest. Especially if you enjoy the sense of creeping doom that this game manage to deliver, and also don't care about any material rewards that you could gain from, say, trying any local vending machines instead.

Initially a free-to-play Zelda-like with hints of Phantasy Star Online, Spiral Knights has, over the years, taken on more aspects of the latter, while dropping those of the former.
For those of you who may have felt burned by the game in those first couple years, I recommend giving the game another shot, as the changes made to core mechanics have been staggering. These changes include small floating companions who you feed items to, who are most certainly _not_ mags, new abilities in the form of an evade roll and a shield bash, a series of storyline missions that manage to reasonably equip and prepare new players for the game proper, and most importantly of all, the elimination of energy as a currency for playing the game.
Spiral Knights has by and large done away with energy, which is now used almost exclusively for the types of microtransactions you'd expect from a free-to-play game. Elevators are now free to use, meaning that the game no longer nickel and dimes you just to play it, though it still requires luck to be able to find the new universal material for crafting items, and items no longer level up as their heat peaks, they too require a new item. Both of these items can be bought for energy. Make of that what you will.
Overall, the changes have been positive, however, and I'd recommend new players and old to give it a shot before passing final judgement upon it.

Overall (8.5/10) :
*********************
This game isn't for the light-hearted and that is what's great about it. If you like really hard challenges and real decision-making on your choices, this is definitely the game for you. This game isn't merciful, isn't kind and won't treat you well, at all...
Prologue :
*********** (Details of the review below, on the next section)
So... There's a lot to talk about in this game. But first, I would like to comment on the recent reviews... All I see are people who give bad and non-constructive critics of the game (i.e. "The game isn't working" or "The game is too hard and the RNG is hateful"). Let me say that the people who says those comments are just buying the game because it's getting more and more attention in the game industry and they didn't take the time to see what they were buying.
Of course, there will be bugs in certain builds of the game, it isn't even finished yet and for the difficulty; one of the big reasons that this game is so satisfying and great IS because it is so god damn hard. So if you are a casual game player (i.e LoL, CoD, etc.) just don't play it (You need to accept defeat in this game to move forward and succeed). Okay... now I can start my review...
Graphics (8/10) :
******************
The graphics in this game really corresponds with it's whole atmosphere. It's dark, it's scary, it's beautiful. The only thing that I can say about it is that it lacks a bit of different animations in the attacks, misses, dodges, etc. But hey, it's not even finished yet, they might add more graphical content some day.
Gameplay (8.5/10) :
*******************
The gameplay is just amazing. For a nerd of dungeon games, this is just ecstasy. The whole stress system is incredible, it brings the whole "human" put into the characters of the game. The classic protection, damage, dodge, etc. system in the game is just a must have in almost every game and they nailed it so well. If you are a nerd of dungeon games, this is definitely the game for you. I just love how one character can bring the whole group into chaos and anarchy, just because he became paranoid or selfish. It shows how important each character you put into the group plays an important role surviving the dungeon. You must really think hard when building your group for the dungeon expedition. You can't just put a rookie in a team of advanced characters, that rookie can bring down everyone. I also love the fact that when you go out on a mission, you already know that the chances of succeeding are really slim and it just becomes a loot mission just to not loose too much gold on the expedition.
Game Time (9.5/10) :
**********************
This game is so hard, that it just puts it's lifespan far off. And with all the character compositions and number of almost impossible quests that are available just makes the whole adventure even more thrilling than ever. (This game isn't even finished yet?!?!?! Can't wait for more content.)
Sound (6.5/10) :
***************
I would say the sound is "good enough". I feel that it doesn't fulfil the role of immersing the player into the dungeon, if you know what I mean. It they could do a soundtrack that really scares the crap out of the player, this game would be perfect.
Story (6/10) :
**************
The story is okay. But no more. It lacks depth and details on the origin of the horrors in which I would love to know more about. But at the end you realise that you are the one building your own story on how you defeated the evil within.
Until now, this game just gave me great satisfaction on my succeeded missions.

Second game? Definetely PvP.

Invasions? Prepare to Die within 30 seconds, because noone will go online without at least one summon. Here we also have the problem of hacking, gankers who used Dried Fingers (an item that lets you get invaded easier/more often) cheesing you for the souls or the disrespect, turtling hosts with overleveled or hacking summons, and the lag...
The latency compensation in this game is abysmal. I recently parried a host, the damage of his attack still came through and killed me, but he got into the parried animation (2 seconds later).
Or you can't even hit people if they are not right in front of you.
This game's latency compensation and range detection/range processing definetely lacks.
And it tends to tilt the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of me, so that is one of the reasons that I didn't play this much yet.
The story? I couldn't really dig into it, because I felt like the backstory (given through previous titles) was more interesting and important to the game than the actual problem
.
And playing for yourself while challenging yourself with a specific build or boss order gets dull.
Would I recommend this?
If you're a big fan of the series, yes.
If you're a beginner, yes.
If you only feel you need to because you played the previous ones?
Consider buying it only on discount, because my 35 hours don't feel like they're worth 40 bucks.
Or maybe I'm just getting tired of gaming.

This game could well have been one of the best there is, but it's simply not.
Design, concept, and even the level of difficulty is just perfect and adds up to make for a really good game, if only...
If only there was some slightest resemblance of tactics to it that would actually matter to the game play whatsoever!
In the end of the day it all comes down to pure, basic luck whether you make it through even your very first dungeon at all.
Every single attempt of making up a strategy will simply result in nothing but frustration as your characters get pummelled by the lowliest of enemies avaible. And in the same way, your worst attempt ever at making a fully functional party may well come out on top and completely unharmed.
There is simply no consistency to this at all, and it seems like the very design - and not just the gloomy story - has been specifically created to bring you down.
It's one thing to make a game that's simply difficult to master, and something else entirely to make this difficulty simply based on whether your characters are lucky to survive a hit that can range from anywhere between 1 and 21 in damage, or simply happen to get "ambushed" by an enemy that you're already perfectly aware of...
On the other hand, if you actually enjoy being utterly frustrated, or simply want to test your luck at games, then this just might be able to pick your interest. Especially if you enjoy the sense of creeping doom that this game manage to deliver, and also don't care about any material rewards that you could gain from, say, trying any local vending machines instead.

Overall (8.5/10) :
*********************
This game isn't for the light-hearted and that is what's great about it. If you like really hard challenges and real decision-making on your choices, this is definitely the game for you. This game isn't merciful, isn't kind and won't treat you well, at all...
Prologue :
*********** (Details of the review below, on the next section)
So... There's a lot to talk about in this game. But first, I would like to comment on the recent reviews... All I see are people who give bad and non-constructive critics of the game (i.e. "The game isn't working" or "The game is too hard and the RNG is hateful"). Let me say that the people who says those comments are just buying the game because it's getting more and more attention in the game industry and they didn't take the time to see what they were buying.
Of course, there will be bugs in certain builds of the game, it isn't even finished yet and for the difficulty; one of the big reasons that this game is so satisfying and great IS because it is so god damn hard. So if you are a casual game player (i.e LoL, CoD, etc.) just don't play it (You need to accept defeat in this game to move forward and succeed). Okay... now I can start my review...
Graphics (8/10) :
******************
The graphics in this game really corresponds with it's whole atmosphere. It's dark, it's scary, it's beautiful. The only thing that I can say about it is that it lacks a bit of different animations in the attacks, misses, dodges, etc. But hey, it's not even finished yet, they might add more graphical content some day.
Gameplay (8.5/10) :
*******************
The gameplay is just amazing. For a nerd of dungeon games, this is just ecstasy. The whole stress system is incredible, it brings the whole "human" put into the characters of the game. The classic protection, damage, dodge, etc. system in the game is just a must have in almost every game and they nailed it so well. If you are a nerd of dungeon games, this is definitely the game for you. I just love how one character can bring the whole group into chaos and anarchy, just because he became paranoid or selfish. It shows how important each character you put into the group plays an important role surviving the dungeon. You must really think hard when building your group for the dungeon expedition. You can't just put a rookie in a team of advanced characters, that rookie can bring down everyone. I also love the fact that when you go out on a mission, you already know that the chances of succeeding are really slim and it just becomes a loot mission just to not loose too much gold on the expedition.
Game Time (9.5/10) :
**********************
This game is so hard, that it just puts it's lifespan far off. And with all the character compositions and number of almost impossible quests that are available just makes the whole adventure even more thrilling than ever. (This game isn't even finished yet?!?!?! Can't wait for more content.)
Sound (6.5/10) :
***************
I would say the sound is "good enough". I feel that it doesn't fulfil the role of immersing the player into the dungeon, if you know what I mean. It they could do a soundtrack that really scares the crap out of the player, this game would be perfect.
Story (6/10) :
**************
The story is okay. But no more. It lacks depth and details on the origin of the horrors in which I would love to know more about. But at the end you realise that you are the one building your own story on how you defeated the evil within.
Until now, this game just gave me great satisfaction on my succeeded missions.
Wow... This is actually a long review, time for me to go and try to beat some dungeons!!!! :D
I hope this review was useful for someone! :D

Ok so while I really like the game and the general idea there are couple reason why I will again give this a negative review. Yes, the game is a challenge, the game is tactic based and yes the game has a big replay value until a certain point. While you might feel you mastered the dynamics, the trinkets/spells/camping setup, the RNG and unbalanced minions will eventually beat you after you start doing the champion challenges. You might feel that everything is doing fine after you realize that the minions stats do not really scale with your heroes stats meaning that the higher level you get, the lower damage you deal due to the fact that every minion now has ridiculou dodge/prot/crit ratings which makes the no longer a challenge but a dice roll. The size 2 minions can one shot you with non crit atacks (treebranch smackdown from the troll hits for 30+ non crit, 55+ crit), the bleed/blight now deals an insane amount of damage per turn while the game absolutely ignores your resists. I have for example 90%+ on both bleed and blight but I would still only resists those kind of atacks about 2/10 times. As for today I lost 4  lvl 6 characters in only an hour gameplay (dont have to mention how long it takes to pimp out your heroes) because I just wouldnt beat the dice rolls (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ instagibs, bleed/blight dealing 12 per tick..) which makes it utterly frustrating experience. There is just still so much work to be done on this game and if you dont want to rage destroy your rig I suggest you play something where only your decisions and skills have the impact on the game. This game so far is fairly both luck based and improperly mechanized while being pretty unrewarding at the same time.
I am pretty sure that once proper changes are made this game will kick asses but as for now that is not the case. It is still early acces so I do have high hopes for this.

Well, I do recommend this game, however I have to confess that I have had the pleasure of modding the game, and that to me is what makes this Fallout a must have.
I'll make this a quickish review:
Reason why I bought the game:
Loved New Vegas, enjoy the Fallout Universe immensly.
Managed to get with a 60% discount
Best RPG/Open world experience.
It's Fallout, Baby!
Things that shocked/surprised me:
Only one companion can follow you at a time (turns out this was a U-turn made late on by the devs, and mods allow you to have more. [ IMO, I will always have Dogmeat by my side, but realised I was missing story / dialouge from the many other companions] - head to nexus mods for this)
Armor / Weapons don't degrade like in N.V. - In N.V I liked the fact that after a while you'd need to think about getting new / repairing or you could end up in a tight spot. All that's gone in F4, and to me it's a shame as it helped with the whole wasteland vibe.
Settlements -
I assume this was "a key feature" that the devs wanted to show off. IT CAN BE useful, depending on your play through, but for me - I hate it, I don't really care, I'm not interested in re-building (for one its tedious and bloody awkward to get things to place ok, and two boring) - While I have quite a few settlements, I don't even care for any of them... I just have my home base in Diamond City and screw the rest of the populace.
While this is the play through I have choosen, I can't see myself ever enjoying settlement building. I would rather spend my time crafting weapons and armour.
The feel of the game, to me N/V asthetic is waaaay more wasteland feely, don't get me wrong you still are very much in a Fallout Game, and everywhere is devasted. It just doesn't give the same feel of N/V, it's not meant too as your in the commonwealth. I just feel as though things here feel a little more casual, I'm not being pulled into to how drastic the situation is, in fact the commonwealth is doing quite well.
NO factions/Karma
Another thing I miss, there's no real karma system in the game. As such I don't tend to feel remorse for my actions. At times it can make you feel a little detached from the situation you are in, and well I end up double/triple crossing most people to benefit myself. I just don't really seem to be able to♥♥♥♥♥♥anybody off. That being said I haven't gone on a killing spree or anything like that, but I can't see how I would be punished long term if I did..... (Factions are in the game, but there's no real system of being liked/disliked). One good example is a side quest which gives you the choice to seriously feck up a would be companions business, and even if you do go through with it, they still forgive you. The game is all about getting companions to like you. Which is another reason for having the dogmeat + companion mod(fix).
The Companions themselves are interesting, but the like/dislike mechanic can become a little tedious.
Things I like about the game:
I can still do what I want, thankfully your not punished if you're like me and CBA with settlement building. It's still about exploring, meeting wierd and wonderful wasteland critters, and the game is very fleshed out.
The story, I've not compelted  the main story line it, to be honest I could be way off, I'm 85 hours in, with very little, maybe an hour of that setting up graphics and making mods work in game. The part that I am at in the story has got me thinking which way to go, so I'm doing some side quests/exploring while I get myself ready. You never feel bored doing quests which is very important.
My character - again from mods, I have a character that I've taken from pre-war to grimey hard on the outside putting on a brave face all out destoryer of everything, and it's quite compelling that it makes me feel that the actions/choices and events that unfold would make my character act in this way. She's kickass.
It's still fallout, if you're a fan them its a must have. Sure it play slightly different to N/V, but I wouldn't say in a bad way.
Things I haven't found all that great:
Power Armour - Sure it looks great, and well it is bad♥♥♥♥♥ It's just so common. (You can literally find one near the start of the game, without doing any quests) It's really not hard to maintain and gather fusion cores, by the time I got my T-60 from a certain faction in the game, I just stopped caring. It can come in handy when facing enemies en-mass, but I find currently I can take on most enemies with ease (normal difficulty is too easy), my melee perks and weapons are over powered, so being in Power Armor is a little over kill.
I will need it from time to time, it's just not something I hold as a must have. (I'm relying on my characters perks, weapons and armor to combat foes). I think my next outing in it will be to a place I have already scouted out, and armed with my fat man and minigun, should make light work of a certain area. - It's very good when used tactically.
Settlements - I mentioned this before, they just take all the fun out of it for me. I've followed the quest line that allows me to keep on founding new ones, but I pretty much just let them die out. They do have benefits, but the whole gathering on materials bore me to tears (I'll use them on my own kit thank you very much)
Only Charisma Skill checks, another poor choice by the devs.
So a quick summary:
Buy it if you love fallout
Buy it if you love openworld/adventure/rpg
After 10 hours or so in, I had to mod it, nothing to cheat, mostly aesthitics/character development/companion w/ dogmeat/clothing/ texture mods etc. - Not necessary but just gives it that extra something.
If you are thinking about it, look for a discount, I did.
I'll update this again in 50 hours. I aim to be finished by then.
Performance.
I only have a A10 APU, slight O.C as on stock cooler, (but modded case with good air cooling)
I get 40 FPS mostly, dips to 25 in Diamond City but not all that often. I'm playing on Ultra with some textures tweaked. I must mention I am on 720p not 1080, if 1080 I get around 18 to 24FPS.

This game is dark and sometimes can be disturbing. But that doesnt push me away from the very amazing game that I procured. The darkest dungeon so far has an amazing amount of content. My adventurers seem to hate me most of the time as I have been the reason for their comrades demise time and time again. When I believe I have finally gotten together the right party and been able to build them up. Suddenly I have lost two of my most prized heroes due to them panicking. This game is difficult but it rewards you greatly for gaining a win and you feel very accomplished. I enjoy this game and look forward to future updates!
EDIT:
As of now I have put some time into the game and don't believe the comments of other players. I have stuck with this game for some time and for some reason the many hours of gameplay I have put into this game doesn't show on my steam time. I would definattely like to support my original review and have been proven that preparedness AND skill can overcome any "imbalences." This game might have it's shares of bugs at times but the developers are quick to work out the kinks.
Okay, down to the nitty gritty review:
This game WILL challenge you. You WILL lose heroes and you WILL struggle.
BUT, when you finally clear an area, upgrade your manor, get new heroes, upgrade gear and skills. All these things make you feel rewarded for your efforts and careful planning. If you are failing a quest, run then return later with a different party for a different outcome. As your gold supplies dwindle you are forced to take actions, make some sacrifices, or restart a time or two. Careful planning of your heroe's stats, skills, positive, and negative traits should be taken into account when you set out. While lucky rolls and such will have an effect, your skills at running and knowing when enough is enough will ultimately save you and your heroes. This game is a masterpiece and I challenge anyone to test it out for themselves.
End note: if you played dark souls games but wished you could have a party of players, then this might be a good match up for you. Death WILL be common and failure WILL come. But perservere and the rewards will be great. Overall great gameplay, great art, and good stories.

I read the earlier reviews, and I like a challenge, so I thought, "what the hell? I'll give it a go."
No, do not. It is brutual, right out of the gates.
Fatal actually - you have ZERO chance of surviving. You will not finish this game, you won't even finish a chapter. Not for lack of skill or planning however. Read on.
I'm hoping perhaps a patch in the future will resolve this - but as it currently stands, the game is impossible.
PLAYABLITY ISSUES: There is no "recovery" once in the dungeon - where you could fight to a certain spot, then return to town and resupply or recuperate. A rational person would say, "we can't go on, we must retreat." Retreat means failure and penalty. And the mission cannot be reattempted. It's first try, or fail.
It's a death match to the end of every mission - and because so much of the game mechanic  depends on random chance and blind luck, even a well prepared party can have one bad battle, and  literally be doomed.
INTERACTIVE ITEMS: Don't bother, my experience was 99% were traps, diseases, or stress inducing maladies inflicted upon my party. that these typically occur right before a battle was no accident either.
I was badly injured, defeated before the fight even began. Did I mention there is no retreat to recuperate?
Want to start a fight poisoned, blighted, or bleeding to death? Go ahead and open that book, crate, or sarcoghagus.
RANDOM LUCK, NO SKILL INVOLVED: As others have stated here earlier, you can go through a fight with out a scratch against a superior opponent, only to be taken apart by a pack of maggots that all score critical hits the next fight. It's maddening.
There is no healing AFTER battle, (And your healers forgo offense to heal during) heavy wounds give a variety of diseases and stress-related offenses, and of course nothing tops the battle where a necromancer hit my entire party with a massive stress-inducing spell ("6 feet under") and they ALL died due to heart attack. In the same round...simultaneously. Wheee....
On many missions you can camp - ONCE - and recover a slight amount - but you'll never return to proper fighting form. If I was lucky, I might get back to about 50% of my original strength. And this was typically after 2-3 fights!
VERDICT: This game shows a lot of promise, but currently the game mechanic renders it  unplayable.
I'll leave it in my library for a bit and see if there's a patch in the near future.
Otherwise, it's done.

I hadn't played in quite a while due to the feel that it was more of a chore than a game, but I decided to give it a bit more of a go. There's a mechanic that has been added to hero stress since I played last, which feels like a massive kick in the teeth at this point. Now not only do characters max out their stress bar and develop what is usually a mental illness or other negative character trait that requires time and money to cure, but the maxed out bar can now fill up a second time and give the character a heart attack if it fills the bar again. And now there are corpses left to keep enemy positions the same, whereas before they would move up when allies died. You have to go through their hit points again (if you want to waste your already precious time) to get rid of them. I'm sorry, but... whuh?
So... now the game is pretty much unplayable. It was already frustrating when it took a lot of time to mash groups of garbage heroes through dungeons and chuck them after, waiting until there was enough money to take my good groups into dungeons so they could finally get some xp (which is literally THE strategy for getting anywhere in this game)... now it's just gratuitous punishment and a complete waste of time. So very disappointing.

It's an unforgiving game.  Some of the mechanics are flat out unfair.  If one of your party members go down in a fight, the rest of them basically go crazy and become uncontrollable.
Turn order isn't defined clearly.  At the beginning of each round everyone gets a stipend.  The game randomly selects who goes next, and that player loses their stipend.  The only way to strategize is to see who still has theirs (who can still act)
If you're counting on your healer to take his turn next, but the monsters all still have their actions, forget it.
I ~LOVED~ this game until I got my three different parties all up to level 3.  They all started dying one by one, and it was too much of a chore to raise another party through the ranks.
Despite all this, I still like the game.  I think it's very niche, but if it looks like you'd enjoy it, buy it!
But if you are easily frustrated, stay away.

Darkest Dungeon is in a couple of words: Fresh, Thoughtful, and Punishing.
This game really stands out from other games genres you could try to pitch it into. It has roguelike elements in that the dungeons are randomized, but the adventure isn't over when you die. It's a dungeon crawler, but not a Skinner's Box. It's a football manager but instead your players are fighting shrieking pigs and terminal disease. I find it a wonderful combination of many different styles of games, all of those styles blend really well together to form the end product, and none feel forced.
That said, this game can be brutal. The game even tells you before you begin that your characters will die and missions will fail and that the player needs to understand that it's supposed to happen. It adds a new level to the idea that game over is not a fail-state. I found myself when I first started this game restarting over and over, since my first couple of dungeon runs wound up with bad luck. This was frustrating, so I decided instead to roll with the punches and then my experience felt much more bleak but also more rewarding. Tenacity is what this game rewards you for. Understanding when to cut your losses is critical. I digress.

This is a game where you have stranded in an alien world. The goal of the game is to explore this world by following in the footsteps of an missing squad. Missions are give to you from Spiral HQ trough a comlink.
There is also arcade missions based off different story missions. The arcade rotates the missions that can be played weekly. There is also daily missions that you can do for extra prestige (XP). Sometimes limited time events appear that might give rare loot.
Playing this game will quickly feel grindy, due to the fact that the same maps are recycled a lot. You usually meet different enemies, but the levels still feel too simular. It's also hard to gather and level up good equipment, due to the cost and time needed to upgrade equipment.
There is a in-game store where you can spend a currency called "Energy". Energy can be purchased using real world money. The game might for some feel a bit "pay to progress" because you can buy good equipment instantly once you reach the required level for this gear. The great thing with energy is that you can trade it from other players for "Crowns" which is a currency that drops in levels. You can therefor get all the energy you want without spending real life money, as long as you have enough crowns and there are players submiting offers.
This game is programmed mostly in Java. The bad thing about Java is that it uses "virtual machines" for running code. That means that this game will suffer a little bit on the performance part due to the VM overhead. This is usually not a problem with this game due to it's low resource usage.
This game have one DLC. The DLC contains one additional mission called "Operation Crimson hammer". This mission is different than the other missions you can play. It's more challenging than the other missions, but also more fun.
The fact that this game doesn't have tons of expensive DLC's is great!
Finding a game party to play is usually hard and many players choose to play solo. There is also a few players that will kick you once you join, because they do not know how to create private parties. There is also a few mad players that you should watch out for.
This game can give you quite some time of entertainment, if you enjoy playing the same missions over and over again with new and more challenging monsters each time. This game is not "pay to win" and do not have a tons of expensive DLC's. This game is not recommended for people that always want something new.

Well, I do recommend this game, however I have to confess that I have had the pleasure of modding the game, and that to me is what makes this Fallout a must have.
I'll make this a quickish review:
Reason why I bought the game:
Loved New Vegas, enjoy the Fallout Universe immensly.
Managed to get with a 60% discount
Best RPG/Open world experience.
It's Fallout, Baby!
Things that shocked/surprised me:
Only one companion can follow you at a time (turns out this was a U-turn made late on by the devs, and mods allow you to have more. [ IMO, I will always have Dogmeat by my side, but realised I was missing story / dialouge from the many other companions] - head to nexus mods for this)
Armor / Weapons don't degrade like in N.V. - In N.V I liked the fact that after a while you'd need to think about getting new / repairing or you could end up in a tight spot. All that's gone in F4, and to me it's a shame as it helped with the whole wasteland vibe.
Settlements -
I assume this was "a key feature" that the devs wanted to show off. IT CAN BE useful, depending on your play through, but for me - I hate it, I don't really care, I'm not interested in re-building (for one its tedious and bloody awkward to get things to place ok, and two boring) - While I have quite a few settlements, I don't even care for any of them... I just have my home base in Diamond City and screw the rest of the populace.
While this is the play through I have choosen, I can't see myself ever enjoying settlement building. I would rather spend my time crafting weapons and armour.
The feel of the game, to me N/V asthetic is waaaay more wasteland feely, don't get me wrong you still are very much in a Fallout Game, and everywhere is devasted. It just doesn't give the same feel of N/V, it's not meant too as your in the commonwealth. I just feel as though things here feel a little more casual, I'm not being pulled into to how drastic the situation is, in fact the commonwealth is doing quite well.
NO factions/Karma
Another thing I miss, there's no real karma system in the game. As such I don't tend to feel remorse for my actions. At times it can make you feel a little detached from the situation you are in, and well I end up double/triple crossing most people to benefit myself. I just don't really seem to be able to♥♥♥♥♥♥anybody off. That being said I haven't gone on a killing spree or anything like that, but I can't see how I would be punished long term if I did..... (Factions are in the game, but there's no real system of being liked/disliked). One good example is a side quest which gives you the choice to seriously feck up a would be companions business, and even if you do go through with it, they still forgive you. The game is all about getting companions to like you. Which is another reason for having the dogmeat + companion mod(fix).
The Companions themselves are interesting, but the like/dislike mechanic can become a little tedious.
Things I like about the game:
I can still do what I want, thankfully your not punished if you're like me and CBA with settlement building. It's still about exploring, meeting wierd and wonderful wasteland critters, and the game is very fleshed out.
The story, I've not compelted  the main story line it, to be honest I could be way off, I'm 85 hours in, with very little, maybe an hour of that setting up graphics and making mods work in game. The part that I am at in the story has got me thinking which way to go, so I'm doing some side quests/exploring while I get myself ready. You never feel bored doing quests which is very important.
My character - again from mods, I have a character that I've taken from pre-war to grimey hard on the outside putting on a brave face all out destoryer of everything, and it's quite compelling that it makes me feel that the actions/choices and events that unfold would make my character act in this way. She's kickass.
It's still fallout, if you're a fan them its a must have. Sure it play slightly different to N/V, but I wouldn't say in a bad way.
Things I haven't found all that great:
Power Armour - Sure it looks great, and well it is bad♥♥♥♥♥ It's just so common. (You can literally find one near the start of the game, without doing any quests) It's really not hard to maintain and gather fusion cores, by the time I got my T-60 from a certain faction in the game, I just stopped caring. It can come in handy when facing enemies en-mass, but I find currently I can take on most enemies with ease (normal difficulty is too easy), my melee perks and weapons are over powered, so being in Power Armor is a little over kill.
I will need it from time to time, it's just not something I hold as a must have. (I'm relying on my characters perks, weapons and armor to combat foes). I think my next outing in it will be to a place I have already scouted out, and armed with my fat man and minigun, should make light work of a certain area. - It's very good when used tactically.
Settlements - I mentioned this before, they just take all the fun out of it for me. I've followed the quest line that allows me to keep on founding new ones, but I pretty much just let them die out. They do have benefits, but the whole gathering on materials bore me to tears (I'll use them on my own kit thank you very much)
Only Charisma Skill checks, another poor choice by the devs.
So a quick summary:
Buy it if you love fallout
Buy it if you love openworld/adventure/rpg
After 10 hours or so in, I had to mod it, nothing to cheat, mostly aesthitics/character development/companion w/ dogmeat/clothing/ texture mods etc. - Not necessary but just gives it that extra something.
If you are thinking about it, look for a discount, I did.
I'll update this again in 50 hours. I aim to be finished by then.

It's an unforgiving game.  Some of the mechanics are flat out unfair.  If one of your party members go down in a fight, the rest of them basically go crazy and become uncontrollable.
Turn order isn't defined clearly.  At the beginning of each round everyone gets a stipend.  The game randomly selects who goes next, and that player loses their stipend.  The only way to strategize is to see who still has theirs (who can still act)
If you're counting on your healer to take his turn next, but the monsters all still have their actions, forget it.
I ~LOVED~ this game until I got my three different parties all up to level 3.  They all started dying one by one, and it was too much of a chore to raise another party through the ranks.
Despite all this, I still like the game.  I think it's very niche, but if it looks like you'd enjoy it, buy it!
But if you are easily frustrated, stay away.

SCENE I. King Lear's palace.
Enter KENT, GLOUCESTER, and EDMUND
KENT
I thought the king had more affected the Duke of
Albany than Cornwall.
GLOUCESTER
It did always seem so to us: but now, in the
division of the kingdom, it appears not which of
the dukes he values most; for equalities are so
weighed, that curiosity in neither can make choice
of either's moiety.
KENT
Is not this your son, my lord?
GLOUCESTER
His breeding, sir, hath been at my charge: I have
so often blushed to acknowledge him, that now I am
brazed to it.
KENT
I cannot conceive you.
GLOUCESTER
Sir, this young fellow's mother could: whereupon
she grew round-wombed, and had, indeed, sir, a son
for her cradle ere she had a husband for her bed.
Do you smell a fault?
KENT
I cannot wish the fault undone, the issue of it
being so proper.
GLOUCESTER
But I have, sir, a son by order of law, some year
elder than this, who yet is no dearer in my account:
though this knave came something saucily into the
world before he was sent for, yet was his mother
fair; there was good sport at his making, and the
♥♥♥♥♥son must be acknowledged. Do you know this
noble gentleman, Edmund?
EDMUND
No, my lord.
GLOUCESTER
My lord of Kent: remember him hereafter as my
honourable friend.
EDMUND
My services to your lordship.
KENT
I must love you, and sue to know you better.
EDMUND
Sir, I shall study deserving.
GLOUCESTER
He hath been out nine years, and away he shall
again. The king is coming.
Sennet. Enter KING LEAR, CORNWALL, ALBANY, GONERIL, REGAN, CORDELIA, and Attendants
KING LEAR
Attend the lords of France and Burgundy, Gloucester.
GLOUCESTER
I shall, my liege.
Exeunt GLOUCESTER and EDMUND
KING LEAR
Meantime we shall express our darker purpose.
Give me the map there. Know that we have divided
In three our kingdom: and 'tis our fast intent
To shake all cares and business from our age;
Conferring them on younger strengths, while we
Unburthen'd crawl toward death. Our son of Cornwall,
And you, our no less loving son of Albany,
We have this hour a constant will to publish
Our daughters' several dowers, that future strife
May be prevented now. The princes, France and Burgundy,
Great rivals in our youngest daughter's love,
Long in our court have made their amorous sojourn,
And here are to be answer'd. Tell me, my daughters,--
Since now we will divest us both of rule,
Interest of territory, cares of state,--
Which of you shall we say doth love us most?
That we our largest bounty may extend
Where nature doth with merit challenge. Goneril,
Our eldest-born, speak first.
GONERIL
Sir, I love you more than words can wield the matter;
Dearer than eye-sight, space, and liberty;
Beyond what can be valued, rich or rare;
No less than life, with grace, health, beauty, honour;
As much as child e'er loved, or father found;
A love that makes breath poor, and speech unable;
Beyond all manner of so much I love you.
CORDELIA
[Aside] What shall Cordelia do?
Love, and be silent.
LEAR
Of all these bounds, even from this line to this,
With shadowy forests and with champains rich'd,
With plenteous rivers and wide-skirted meads,
We make thee lady: to thine and Albany's issue
Be this perpetual. What says our second daughter,
Our dearest Regan, wife to Cornwall? Speak.
REGAN
Sir, I am made
Of the self-same metal that my sister is,
And prize me at her worth. In my true heart
I find she names my very deed of love;
Only she comes too short: that I profess
Myself an enemy to all other joys,
Which the most precious square of sense possesses;
And find I am alone felicitate
In your dear highness' love.
CORDELIA
[Aside] Then poor Cordelia!
And yet not so; since, I am sure, my love's
More richer than my tongue.
KING LEAR
To thee and thine hereditary ever
Remain this ample third of our fair kingdom;
No less in space, validity, and pleasure,
Than that conferr'd on Goneril. Now, our joy,
Although the last, not least; to whose young love
The vines of France and milk of Burgundy
Strive to be interess'd; what can you say to draw
A third more opulent than your sisters? Speak.
CORDELIA
Nothing, my lord.
KING LEAR
Nothing!
CORDELIA
Nothing.
KING LEAR
Nothing will come of nothing: speak again.
CORDELIA
Unhappy that I am, I cannot heave
My heart into my mouth: I love your majesty
According to my bond; nor more nor less.
KING LEAR
How, how, Cordelia! mend your speech a little,
Lest it may mar your fortunes.
CORDELIA
Good my lord,
You have begot me, bred me, loved me: I
Return those duties back as are right fit,
Obey you, love you, and most honour you.
Why have my sisters husbands, if they say
They love you all? Haply, when I shall wed,
That lord whose hand must take my plight shall carry
Half my love with him, half my care and duty:
Sure, I shall never marry like my sisters,
To love my father all.
KING LEAR
But goes thy heart with this?
CORDELIA
Ay, good my lord.
KING LEAR
So young, and so untender?
CORDELIA
So young, my lord, and true.
KING LEAR
Let it be so; thy truth, then, be thy dower:
For, by the sacred radiance of the sun,
The mysteries of Hecate, and the night;
By all the operation of the orbs
From whom we do exist, and cease to be;
Here I disclaim all my paternal care,
Propinquity and property of blood,
And as a stranger to my heart and me
Hold thee, from this, for ever. The barbarous Scythian,
Or he that makes his generation messes
To gorge his appetite, shall to my bosom
Be as well neighbour'd, pitied, and relieved,
As thou my sometime daughter.
KENT
Good my liege,--
KING LEAR
Peace, Kent!
Come not between the dragon and his wrath.
I loved her most, and thought to set my rest
On her kind nursery. Hence, and avoid my sight!
So be my grave my peace, as here I give
Her father's heart from her! Call France; who stirs?
Call Burgundy. Cornwall and Albany,
With my two daughters' dowers digest this third:
Let pride, which she calls plainness, marry her.
I do invest you jointly with my power,
Pre-eminence, and all the large effects
That troop with majesty. Ourself, by monthly course,
With reservation of an hundred knights,
By you to be sustain'd, shall our abode
Make with you by due turns. Only we still retain
The name, and all the additions to a king;
The sway, revenue, execution of the rest,
Beloved sons, be yours: which to confirm,
This coronet part betwixt you.
Giving the crown
KENT
Royal Lear,
Whom I have ever honour'd as my king,
Loved as my father, as my master follow'd,
As my great patron thought on in my prayers,--
KING LEAR
The bow is bent and drawn, make from the shaft.
KENT
Let it fall rather, though the fork invade
The region of my heart: be Kent unmannerly,
When Lear is mad. What wilt thou do, old man?
Think'st thou that duty shall have dread to speak,
When power to flattery bows? To plainness honour's bound,
When majesty stoops to folly. Reverse thy doom;
And, in thy best consideration, cheque
This hideous rashness: answer my life my judgment,
Thy youngest daughter does not love thee least;
Nor are those empty-hearted whose low sound
Reverbs no hollowness.
KING LEAR
Kent, on thy life, no more.
KENT
My life I never held but as a pawn
To wage against thy enemies; nor fear to lose it,
Thy safety being the motive.
KING LEAR
Out of my sight!
KENT
